subject: Token rounding simulation results + proposed invoice safeguard language
messages:

Subject: Clarify rounding/minimums impact for pilot invoicing

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the call earlier — quick follow-up from procurement. We have two outstanding concerns before we sign the pilot SOW: token rounding behavior for streaming calls, and how small-session minimums interact with our monthly invoice. Specifically:

- When a user streams short prompts repeatedly (think 6–12 tokens responses), does Redwood round each call up to the microfloor or aggregate across minute windows?
- If we exceed the commit only in bursts, do you apply a minimum per-call floor or a per-session/month floor?

We ran a quick internal projection and the different options change our estimated TCO by ~12–18%. Can you send the simulation you mentioned and a short paragraph we can put in the SOW around invoice safeguards/penalty caps? Legal wants explicit language so they can sign off.

Attached: none from our side yet — procurement wants the numbers first.

Appreciate it,

Talia Brooks
Director of Procurement, EngageCorp
T: (415) 555-0198

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Talia Brooks <talia@engagecorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify rounding/minimums impact for pilot invoicing

Hi Talia — thanks, great questions.

I ran the simulations with Marissa and Serg (attached CSV) and summarized the outcome below. High level: the runtime supports two independent behaviors we can pick per-route:

1) per-call microfloor: rounds up each API request to the nearest microfloor (default for streaming to guarantee cold-response CPU).
2) rolling-window aggregation: aggregates token counts across a configurable time window (default 60s) and applies rounding only to the window total.

Simulation results (attached token_rounding_sim_v2.csv):
- For high-frequency short responses (avg 8 tokens, 1 req/sec), per-call microfloor increases billable tokens by ~16%.
- With rolling-window aggregation (60s), the overhead drops to ~3.4% because small responses get combined.
- If you prefer strict monthly amortization (aggregate all calls per-user per-month) overhead is under 1% in our sample workload.

Proposed pragmatic approach for the pilot:
- Use rolling-window aggregation (60s) for chat endpoints by default.
- Provide an opt-in per-route toggle to the per-call microfloor for latency-critical streaming endpoints.
- Include a monthly reconciliation mode (off by default) that EngageCorp can turn on during invoice review if you need tighter TCO guarantees.

I attached the CSV with the per-route breakdown and a short redline (Marissa drafted) for an invoice safeguard clause. Marissa — adding you to handle the contract paragraph and confirm the exact wording we can commit to.

Next steps:
- Marissa to propose contract language + show sample invoice line that calls out rounding method.
- Serg to confirm any runtime caveats (KV cache interactions) and whether rolling-window causes any measurable latency trade-offs.

Thanks — sending attachments now.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify rounding/minimums impact for pilot invoicing

Hi Talia — draft language and a short rationale below. Attaching the proposed contract paragraph as invoice_safeguard_clause_v1.docx and the simulation CSV (again) for your finance team.

Contract paragraph (draft):
"Invoice Safeguard — Rounding & Aggregation. Redwood Inference will apply token aggregation and rounding according to the mutually selected routing configuration (per-call microfloor, rolling-window aggregation, or monthly amortization). For the initial pilot term, parties agree to use rolling-window aggregation with a 60-second window unless EngageCorp elects per-call microfloor on a per-route basis via written notice. If, after the first two invoices, EngageCorp demonstrates (with Redwood-supplied logs) that rounding or microfloor application caused a billing variance exceeding 5% relative to aggregated token usage under monthly amortization, Redwood will issue a one-time invoice credit equal to 50% of the variance amount, up to a cap of $10,000. The parties may opt to switch to monthly amortization for subsequent invoices upon mutual written agreement."
Why this protects EngageCorp and Redwood:
- Rolling-window reduces noise from repeated short polls while preserving latency SLAs.
- The 5% trigger avoids micro-adjustments from natural tokenization variance but captures meaningful billing regressions.
- The one-time credit + cap keeps our operational exposure bounded and is easy for both sides to audit.

Operational notes:
- We will provide per-invoice token-level CSV exports for the pilot (same format as attached).
- If EngageCorp enables monthly amortization during invoice review, we will run a reconciliation and either issue a credit or invoice adjustment in the next billing cycle.

Serg: can you confirm there are no KV-cache or batching edge cases that would make the 60s window infeasible for any of their main endpoints?

Talia — happy to iterate. If that language looks ok, we can push a DocuSign via the internal link Jonas provided and lock pilot billing behavior.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Marissa / Jonas — thanks for the fast turnaround and the simulation. Procurement + finance ran the CSV and want two small changes before legal will sign:

1) Can the 5% trigger be evaluated after excluding outlier days (defined as days where total daily tokens are below 10% of the 30-day median)? Finance says a single day of very low usage (e.g., staging traffic) could skew the trigger.
2) Can we reduce the credit split to 40% of the variance and raise the cap to $15k (they prefer smaller ongoing credits but a higher overall cap)?

If you accept those, legal will queue signatures and we can start the pilot next week. Also — procurement asked for one short line in the DocuSign to call out the default: "Default billing method during pilot: rolling-window aggregation (60s)."

We'd like the per-invoice CSV included as an attachment to each invoice PDF if possible.

Quick thumbs: I checked the proposed language and it looks operationally reasonable. If you agree, please update the doc and send the DocuSign link.

Thanks,

Talia Brooks
